title: Write a shell script that ranks error codes in a log
instruction:
Write an executable POSIX shell script top_errors.sh. Usage: sh top_errors.sh LOGFILE [N]. app.log is an example log.

An error code is the text ERR- followed by exactly four digits, for example ERR-1042. Matching is case sensitive. A line can contain several codes and every occurrence counts.

Print the N most frequent codes (N defaults to 3), one per line, formatted as CODE COUNT with a single space between them. Order by count descending, and break ties by code ascending. If there are fewer than N distinct codes print them all. If there are none print nothing. Exit with status 0 in these cases.

If LOGFILE cannot be read, print a message to stderr and exit with status 2. Use only standard tools such as grep, sort, uniq, awk and head.
